title: Choose Taracine's new visual world
question: Re-roll 1. Your brief pins modern, aesthetic, easy to use. The roll assigned Kiosk Clarity. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Kiosk Clarity
options.lineage: the self-service ticket kiosk in a modern cinema lobby: one task per screen, oversized touch targets, a step rail, a Continue bar
options.thesis: The website is the kiosk: every course is a single clear step with buttons you could hit with a thumb from arm's length.
materials: one orange accent for the current step and primary action
poster art as the only imagery
Lexend, a face designed for reading ease, everywhere
options.viewport: Slim top bar (wordmark, cinema pill, Sign in). A step rail: 1 Movie · 2 Cinema & time · 3 Tickets, step 1 lit orange. Below it a wall of large poster tiles with title, rating and the next showtime printed on each; tapping one highlights it and a bottom bar slides in: 'Continue with The Lantern Keeper'. Secondary rows (Coming soon, Formats, Cinemas, Club) follow as calm white courses.
options.risk: Can feel like a vending machine if the spacing goes stingy or the orange spreads; the posters must carry the aesthetic.

raised.raise: Sold-out and past showtimes stay visible as tagged gaps, never removed, so the day's shape reads at a glance.
Color rationed by role: orange is only the current step and the primary action, ink is structure, nothing else is colored.
Selection changes weight, not just color: the chosen tile's title steps up a weight and scale.
Every showtime pill carries its own small tag of format and price, so nothing has to be looked up elsewhere.
States print themselves inline (Held for 10 minutes, Not showing here); no toasts, no modals.
One incandescent accent, reserved; hover and active are the only places it brightens.

options.label: Film Magazine
options.lineage: editorial film sites and magazines: white page, big type, poster as the picture, generous whitespace
options.thesis: Taracine reads like a well-designed film magazine that happens to sell tickets.
options.viewport: A big headline 'This week at Taracine', one lead film with its poster at full column height and a short blurb, a tight grid of the rest with showtimes as plain text rows, the finder as a quiet inline form.
options.risk: The most familiar 'modern & aesthetic' landing: beautiful, but the editorial calm can slow a hurried moviegoer, and cobalt sits near the reference's blue.

options.label: Bauhaus Workshop
options.lineage: foundation-course exercises: primary circle, square, triangle on a white worktable, baseline grid
options.thesis: Films and showtimes composed as point, line and plane on a visible grid, primaries rationed by role.
options.viewport: A visible baseline grid, lowercase headlines, poster planes aligned to it; the selected film carries a red disc, showtimes as ruled rows, alerts as small yellow triangles.
options.case: Holds product clarity: ruthless hierarchy and one job per color. Loses on identification: moviegoers do not see themselves in a design-school worktable, and lowercase-only headlines slow reading on phones.
options.risk: Primary colors next to 20 posters get loud fast.

options.label: Video Store Wall
options.thesis: Films as clamshells on a fluorescent shelf.
options.viewport: A wall of spines and face-out boxes under fluorescent light.
options.case: Nostalgic and dark; the opposite of the brief's modern pin.
options.kept: Absences stay visible as tagged gaps.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.lineage: cephalopod skin as a living display
options.thesis: A surface whose pattern travels with state.
options.viewport: Patterns traveling across a cream surface as you select.
options.case: Organic and showy; reads as biology, not a cinema, and the shader cost fights ease.
options.kept: Selection changes type weight, not just color.

options.label: Moon-shadow Bazaar
options.lineage: a surreal night market trading shadows
options.thesis: Films as stalls down a moonlit lane.
options.viewport: Stalls ranked down one lane, each tagged with a ticket.
options.case: Dark, surreal and slow; fails the modern, easy pin.
options.kept: Every item carries its own small origin tag.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminal in a machine room
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript with a breathing cursor.
options.case: Monospace-on-black is the technical costume and unreadable in a bright mall.
options.kept: States print themselves inline, never as chrome.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.lineage: experiential studio portal with a full-screen shader
options.thesis: Thin type floating over living pixels.
options.viewport: A breathing shader with one giant word and tiny links.
options.case: Dark single-hue plus one giant word is the AI-site rut and hides every poster and showtime.
options.kept: One incandescent accent reserved for hover and active.

canonCard.label: The cinema-chain standard
canonCard.thesis: What multiplex and streaming sites ship: dark UI, trailer-still hero, poster carousels, one red Buy Tickets button, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Trailer-still hero with a red CTA, a horizontal poster carousel, Now Showing / Coming Soon tabs, cinema dropdown.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every multiplex site by design.
